doc.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: His own albums and songwriter tributes
summary: His own albums, the Berlin and Arlen LPs, and 'Rhythm and Winds' as his first record.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: That’s interesting. Do you have any idea of how many recordings you played on?

Not really. I have a lot that I played on and I have at least maybe a dozen albums that I had done the arranging and so-called leading on, which are under my own name. Some of them are more of a feature thing like this — or I did a lot of recordings of, this record company was interested in doing mostly songwriters. I never really knew much about songwriters or cared much until working for this record company, Monmouth Evergreen Records, we did three twelve inch LPs of Irving Berlin things on the occasion of his eightieth birthday, so you can see how far back it was. And we did Harold Arlen and quite a few others. But those were in a sense commercial, although they were jazz oriented, they had singers and I did the charts and did playing and stuff. And so there are a lot of those kind of things too, as well as just going unrecognized, whatever the word, and just going in and sitting.
Well I have a list out of one of the jazz recording books and it has your eight or nine recordings between 1955 and ‘65. Those were good years for you.
“Rhythm and Winds” on Esoteric, that was your first recording?
Yes, right. That’s the very first.
Well it says here a mint condition copy is worth a hundred dollars.
